articles.heading: Purpose of these Regulations These Regulations establish licensing requirements and other rules governing the
articles.text:
non-deposit-taking financial services
providers.

articles.heading: Interpretation In these Regulations – (a) “place of business” means a branch, a subbranch or any other place where a
articles.text:
non-deposit-taking financial service
provider carries out some or all its
business;
(b) “Central Bank” means the National
Bank of Rwanda;
(c) “money lending” means the business
of lending money at interest;
(d) “rehabilitation” means restoration of
rights to perform non-deposit taking
financial services after dismissal or
suffering any other sanction imposed
by the Central Bank or any other
institution for misconduct in the
financial sector;
(e) “legal entity” refers to a company,
partnership, cooperative, organisation
or any other organ which is subject of
rights and obligations in accordance
with law;
(f) “development finance institution”
means a financial service provider that
grants loans mainly for economic
development projects;
(g) “finance lease” means a type of loan
whereby a person, the lessee, obtains
the right of possession and use of a
non-monetary asset, owned by another
person, the lessor, for a specific period
during which the lessee pays the agreed
upon lease rental and may acquire
ownership of the asset at the end of the
lease agreement;
(h) “peer-to-peer lending” means a form
of debt-based crowdfunding that uses
online platforms to raise unsecured
loans which are paid back with interest;
(i) “asset finance” refers to a loan that
enables a borrower to acquire an asset
and repay the loan in instalments over
an agreed period;
(j) “pawnshop” means the business of
lending money on security of goods
and in expectation of gain or reward by
taking those goods into their
possession but without taking
ownership of the goods;
(k) “non-performing loan or
commitment” means a loan or
commitment with at least one unpaid
instalment in full or in part within 90
days from the day following the
contractual due date;
(l) “performance security” means a
guarantee issued by an authorised
financial institution to guarantee the
procuring entity that in case the
procurement contract is not well
performed, be it technically or at the
level of deadlines, the procuring entity
receives the amount provided for such
a guarantee;
(m)“haircut” means the difference
between the market value of an asset
used as loan collateral and the amount
of the loan. The amount of the haircut
reflects the lender’s perceived risk of
loss from the asset falling in value at
the market;
(n) “factoring services” means an
agreement by which a financial
intermediary undertakes to purchase
receivables from financial institutions.
Alternatively, a factor can act as
funding source that pays the institution
or an individual the value of the invoice
less a discount for commission and
fees;
(o) “refinancing service” means a
business aimed at addressing the
liquidity shortage in financial service
providers by providing loans to
increase their lending or business
capacity;
(p) “debt collection services” means a
business of collecting and recovering
loans on behalf of a financial service
provider;
(q) “financial services” means the
mortgage finance services, credit
guarantees, refinancing services, peerto-peer lending, money lending
services, factoring services, finance
lease services, pawnshops and any
other service as may be qualified as
such by the Central Bank;
(r) “mortgage finance services” means
lending funds for acquisition of
residential and commercial property
which are principally secured by
mortgages on the financed properties;
(s) “credit guarantee” means a security
or a collateral to the borrower by
covering full or a share of the default
risk of the loan. In case of default, the
lender recovers the value of the
guarantee from the guarantor;
(t) “credit intermediary” means an
institution that acts as a neutral third
party administrator between the
borrower and its lenders supporting a
deal either at closing or later as a
successor intermediary;
(u) “debt counsellor” means a
professional person specialised in
advising debtors or prospective debtors
to manage their debts more
successfully or assist borrowers to
negotiate with their lenders;
(v) “significant shareholder” means a
shareholding in a non-deposit-taking
financial services provider that,
directly or indirectly, alone or in
conjunction with others, represents at
least 5% of the capital or voting rights,
or that makes it possible to exercise a
significant influence over decisions
related to the management of that nondeposit-taking financial service
provider;
(w)“member of Management” means the
management personnel which are the
key executive managers of the nondeposit-taking financial service
provider, including –
(i) the chief executive officer
(CEO)/managing director (MD);
(ii) senior executives reporting to the
Board of Directors or to the Board
Committees;
(iii) senior executive managers
reporting to the chief executive
officer (CEO) or managing director
(MD);
(x) “financial services provider” means
both non-deposit-taking and deposittaking financial service provider as
defined in their respective regulations;
(y) “non-deposit-taking financial
services provider” means a legal
entity other than deposit-taking that has
been licensed by the Central Bank to
provide “financial services” as defined
in these Regulations.

articles.heading: Scope of application (1) These Regulation apply to non-deposittaking financial services providers as
articles.text:
defined in this Regulation and any
other non-deposit-taking financial
service provider not governed by any
other specific law or regulation.
(2) These Regulations do not apply to
sellers that sell their products on
deferred payment.

articles.heading: Categories of non-deposit-taking financial service providers (1) Non-deposit-taking financial services
Application for a license (1) A legal entity intending to provide financial services as non-deposittaking financial services provider
articles.text:
applies in writing to the Central Bank.
(2) A legal entity may apply for a license
to provide financial services as nondeposit-taking financial services
provider in one of the categories
provided for in these Regulations.
(3) An applicant for a license makes a full
description for each service proposed
to be provided depending on the chosen
category.
(4) An applicant for a license to operate as
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider submits to the Central Bank a
licensing application form in Annex I.
(5) The application letter is accompanied
by the following documents:
(a) a filled information sheet for each
significant shareholder, member of
management or Board member in the
form set out in Annex II;
(b) proposed capital structure including
types of shares, share allocation and
complete identifications of
shareholders;
(c) physical address of its proposed head
office and places of business;
(d) a business plan comprising action plan,
business model and financial
projections for at least three years,
including the assumptions underlying
the projections;
(e) the certificate of incorporation;
(f) the memorandum of understanding;
(g) for foreign applicant, a letter of nonobjection from the home supervisory
authority for the establishment of a
subsidiary or branch in Rwanda and a
confirmation from the home supervisor
that it undertakes the consolidated
supervision; where applicable;
(h) a certified copy of the resolutions of the
promoters to establish a non-deposittaking financial services provider;
(i) the relevant policies and procedures;
(j) proof that the applicant for the license
to operate as a non-deposit-taking
financial services provider has the
minimum capital required;
(k) a statement that the invested funds are
not coming from illegal activities as per
Annex III;
(l) any other information that the Central
Bank may deem necessary while
assessing the application.
(6) The submission of untrue or
misleading information constitutes
sufficient grounds for license rejection
or revocation of the license when the
license has been granted.

articles.heading: Specific requirements for a digital credit provider A licensed non-deposit-taking financial
articles.text:
service provider that intends to provide its
credit services digitally shall submit the
following to the Central Bank:
(a) a description of terms and conditions of
credit products and services it intends
to provide;
(b) a description of the information and
communication technology system to
be used in the operations of the digital
credit provider;
(c) agreement with a telecommunication
or other service provider for provision
of channels or platforms for provision
of digital credit;
(d) the proposed digital credit provider’s
data protection policies and
procedures;
(e) the proposed digital credit provider’s
anti-money laundering and combating
the financing of terrorism policies and
procedures;
(f) the credit policy, code of ethics and
market conduct.

articles.heading: Non-refundable application fee The applicant for a license to provide nondeposit-taking financial services pays the
Minimum capital (1) The minimum paid-up capital for a non-deposit-taking financial services
articles.text:
provider is as follows:
(a) 500,000,000 FRW for non-deposittaking financial services provider
under category I;
(b) 200,000,000 FRW for non-deposittaking financial services provider
under category II;
(c) no minimum capital required for
non-deposit-taking financial
service providers under category
III.
(2) The minimum capital specified in
Paragraph (1) may be in cash or in kind
provided that the capital in kind does
not exceed 30% of the total minimum
capital required.
(3) In case the capital is in cash, it is
deposited on a fixed term account in
bank or deposit-taking microfinance
institution established in Rwanda and
the applicant for the license submits the
deposit certificate to the Central Bank
prior to getting the full license.
(4) In case part of the capital is in kind, the
applicant submits to the Central Bank,
the legal evidence of such capital in the
names of the non-deposit-taking
financial service provider and plan to
realize those assets into cash or cash
equivalent or utilize it in the activities
of non-deposit-taking financial service
providers.
(5) The minimum paid-up capital remains
in the bank or deposit-taking
microfinance institution until the non
objection is granted or denied.
(6) The applicant for license demonstrates
the ability to maintain at all times its
unimpaired capital at the prescribed
minimum regulatory capital and to
comply with the established capital
adequacy ratio.
(7) The applicant for the licence submits
the supporting documents evidencing
the sources of capital funds.
(8) The Central Bank may increase the
capital in case the non-deposit-taking
financial services provider needs to
combine activities of more than one
category or depending on any other
reason.

articles.heading: Notice of the receipt of the application (1) The Central Bank notifies the applicant of the license the receipt of the
articles.text:
application within a period of 10
working days from the date of receipt
of application. The Central Bank may
request the applicant to provide
additional or missing information, or to
rectify deficiencies in the application.
(2) The applicant of the license provides
additional or missing information or
rectifies deficiencies in the application
within a period of 30 working days
from the date of request of Central
Bank. If the period is exceeded with no
addition or missing, or rectification in
the application, the application for
license is rejected. However, the
Central Bank may extend the period
upon request by the applicant of the
license.

articles.heading: Central Bank decision The Central Bank analyses the application and issues the decision for granting or not granting
articles.text:
a license, within 30 working days after receipt
of a complete application. Where the Central
Bank grants the license, it issues a license
certificate. In case the license is denied, the
Central Bank provides to the applicant of the
license refusal reasons.

articles.heading: Duration and display of license (1) The license granted remains valid unless suspended or revoked by the
articles.text:
Central Bank on grounds provided for
in these Regulations.
(2) A license certificate granted is always
displayed in a conspicuous place at the
head office of the concerned nondeposit-taking financial services
provider, and copies of it are similarly
displayed at each of its places of
business.

articles.heading: Provision of non-objection (1) When the applicant for a license to provide non-deposit-taking financial
articles.text:
services has fulfilled a significant
portion of the licensing requirements,
the Central Bank may decide to grant a
non-objection to start operations while
waiting for the fulfilment of all
licensing requirements.
(2) The non-objection to start operations
referred to in Paragraph (1) cannot
cover a period of more than 12 months.
In case this period is exceeded without
getting the full license, the Central
Bank may revoke the granted nonobjection.

articles.heading: Foreign company applying for license in Rwanda (1) A foreign company may apply for a license to provide financial services as
articles.text:
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider in form of a subsidiary or a
branch in Rwanda.
(2) In addition to the requirements in

articles.heading: Approval of Board members and members of management (1) Positions of Board members and members of Management of a nondeposit-taking financial services
articles.text:
provider are approved by the Central
Bank.
(2) A non-deposit-taking financial services
provider provides to the Central Bank
the details for each Board member and
member of Management within 30
days of the change or appointment and
must include all elements enabling the
Central Bank to assess the competency,
integrity and good character.
(3) After receipt of a complete application,
the Central Bank informs the nondeposit-taking financial services
provider within a period not exceeding
30 working days on the approved and
rejected Board member or member of
management.

articles.heading: Opening a place of business (1) A licensed non-deposit-taking financial services provider may open
articles.text:
places of business with prior
authorization from the Central Bank.
(2) The request to open a place of business
is submitted in writing to the Central
Bank specifying the following:
(a) the location and nature of activities
envisaged;
A
(b) feasibility study with financial
projections of at least two years;
(c) the proposed staffing structure of
the place of business;
(d) proof of payment of nonrefundable application fee of
50,000 FRW to the Central Bank.
(3) After completion of the required
documents, the Central Bank issues its
decision within a period of 30 working
days.

articles.heading: Acquisition, amalgamation or merger (1) A non-deposit-taking financial services provider subject to acquisition or
articles.text:
intending to amalgamate or merge,
seeks prior authorization from the
Central Bank.
(2) A non-deposit-taking financial
services provider applying for
authorisation for acquisition,
amalgamation or merger, submits to
the Central Bank the following
documents:
(a) application letter addressed to the
Central Bank;
(b) resolutions of the members
adopting the acquisition,
amalgamation or merger;
(c) the contract of acquisition,
amalgamation or merger;
(d) the business model and feasibility
study containing the financial
projections of the acquired,
amalgamated or merged businesses
for at least three years;
(e) the proposed shareholding and
organizational structure of the
acquired, amalgamated or merged
businesses.
(3) After fulfilling the requirements, the
Central Bank issues a decision within a
period of 30 working days.
(4) If the Central Bank denies granting
authorization for acquisition,
amalgamation or merger, it informs the
applicant in writing, of its decision and
the grounds for non-authorization.
CHAPTER III: STRUCTURE AND
OPERATIONS OF NON-DEPOSITTAKING FINANCIAL SERVICE
PROVIDER
Section One: Shareholding, forms of
business and funding sources of a nondeposit-taking financial services provider

articles.heading: Shareholding structure A natural or legal person can own shares in the non-deposit-taking financial services provider
articles.text: up to the tune of 100%.

articles.heading: Acquisition or transfer of shareholding (1) Acquisition or transfer of significant shareholding is approved by the
articles.text:
Central Bank upon the submission of
documents required in Annex II.
(2) The non-deposit-taking financial
services provider further notifies the
Central Bank on any increment of the
shareholding by existing shareholders.
(3) A person who has committed
administrative fault in the financial
institution cannot be a shareholder of a
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider unless rehabilitated by the
Central Bank.

articles.heading: Funding sources of non-deposittaking financial services provider activities (1) The activities of a non-deposit-taking
Forms of businesses of the nondeposit-taking financial services provider The non-deposit-taking financial services
Conducting additional activities The non-deposit-taking financial services provider conducts one or several activities for
articles.text:
which they received licence. In case of a need
to conduct additional activity not previously
licensed for, it applies to the Central Bank with
the following documents:
(a) application letter addressed to the
Central Bank;
(b) resolutions of the Board of Directors or
its equivalent approving the new
activity;
(c) the business model and internal
policies and procedures governing the
new activity.

articles.heading: Combining financial services and non-financial services (1) The non-deposit-taking financial
articles.text:
services provider may combine
financial services with complementary
non-financial services if the financial
service dominates the business of the
non-deposit-taking financial service
provider. For the purpose of this
Regulation, financial services
dominate the business if they represent
at least 70% of the total assets of the
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider.
(2) When the services referred to in the
Paragraph (1) are combined, the nondeposit-taking financial services
provider reports separate and
consolidated financials to the Central
Bank for both financial and nonfinancial service activities.

articles.heading: Strategic documents The non-deposit-taking financial services provider maintains and uses strategic
articles.text:
documents to guide its business as follows:
(a) updated strategic and business plans
and the annual budget;
(b) updated internal policies and
procedures, including administration
and human resources policy, core
business operating policy, investment
policy, accounting and finance policy
as well as other operating policies and
procedures relevant to the business;
(c) risk management framework;
(d) another strategic document that the
Central Bank may deem necessary.

articles.heading: Outsourcing (1) The non-deposit-taking financial services provider can outsource some of its functions or activities if it does
articles.text:
not lead to conflicts of interest.
(2) Any outsourcing of a material function
or activity of the non-deposit-taking
financial services provider requires
approval from the Central Bank.
However, the non-deposit-taking
financial services provider cannot
outsource the function of Board of
Directors and chief executive officer.
(3) The non-deposit-taking financial
services provider applying to outsource
its services, submits to the Central
Bank the following documents:
(a) application letter addressed to the
Central Bank;
(b) details of the service to outsource,
including the persons outsourced to
and how they will run that service;
(c) cost and benefit analysis of
outsourcing that service;
(d) due diligence report conducted
against key individuals who will
perform the outsourced services for
the non-deposit-taking financial
services provider;
(e) any other information that the
Central Bank may request.
Section 3: Relocation or closure of business
and change of name

articles.heading: Relocation or closure of a place of business (1) The non-deposit-taking financial services provider may relocate or
articles.text:
closure a place of business.
(2) Relocation or closure of the place of
business does not require the approval
of the Central Bank but the nondeposit-taking financial services
provider notifies the Central Bank, in
writing, at least ten days before it is
done.
(3) In case of relocation or closure of the
place of business, the non-deposittaking financial services provider
removes all signage from the former
place of business.

articles.heading: Change of corporate name The non-deposit-taking financial services provider that changes the corporate name
articles.text:
notifies the Central Bank thereof in writing.
CHAPTER IV: CORPORATE
GOVERNANCE
Section One: Board of Directors

articles.heading: Composition and qualifications of the Board of Directors (1) A non-deposit-taking financial service
articles.text:
provider must have at least three
directors, with at least two nonexecutive directors for Category I and
one non-executive director for category
II, and the 2/3 of them must possess a
bachelor’s degree in business
management related field. For
Category III, the Board structure and
composition established at
incorporation applies.
(2) If a member of the Board of Director of
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider resides outside the country, he
or she shows how he or she fulfils the
duties of the directorship.
(3) A Board member can serve as a
director in more than one financial
service provider. However, he or she
discloses to the Central Bank that being
a Board member of such institutions
does not lead to conflicts of interest.
(4) A permanent staff serving in the
banking or microfinance sectors in
lending function cannot serve as Board
member in the non-deposit-taking
financial service providers.

articles.heading: Responsibilities and operating conditions of the Board of Directors The responsibilities and other operating
articles.text:
conditions of the Board members are defined
in the Board charter of the non-deposit-taking
financial services provider.

articles.heading: Board Committees The non-deposit-taking financial services provider may establish committees of Board of
articles.text:
Directors.
Section 2: Management

articles.heading: Composition of the Management for categories I and II and qualifications of its members (1) The management of the non-deposittaking financial services provider
articles.text:
headed by the managing director. The
Managing Director must have at least a
bachelor’s degree in business
administration, accounting, economics
or any other qualification relevant to
the business of the non-deposit-taking
financial services provider.
(2) The Managing Director must have at
least two years relevant experience in
the business of the non-deposit-taking
financial services provider or
experience in the financial sector or in
any other field that can help him or her
to run the business of the non-deposittaking financial services provider.
(3) The non-deposit-taking financial
service provider under category I and II
hire sufficient staff depending on the
nature and complexity of the business.
The non-deposit-taking financial
services provider must have at least key
staff in the following core functions:
(a) finance and accounting;
(b) credit;
(c) any other relevant function.
(4) Employees heading core functions of
the non-deposit-taking financial
services provider as defined in the
organizational structure, must have at
least a bachelor’s degree and relevant
experience in the field related to the
function headed.
(5) Duties, working framework and
required qualifications of staff are
defined in human resources
management policy and staff profiles.
(6) A person cannot serve as an employee
of the non-deposit-taking financial
service provider and employee of any
other financial institution.

articles.heading: Management for category III The Directive may determine the Management structure for non-deposit-taking financial
articles.text: service providers under Category III.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Management (1) The Management – (a) ensures that activities of the nondeposit-taking financial services
articles.text:
provider are consistent with the
business strategy, risk appetite, and
policies approved by the Board of
Directors;
(b) ensures that the employees are
adequately trained and able to
perform their duties and
responsibilities.
(2) Members of the Management with
professional certificates undergo
continuing professional development.
However, non-certified members of the
management undergo continuous
training relevant to their roles.
(3) The management is responsible for
ensuring that appropriate and timely
actions are taken on all internal audit
findings and recommendations.

articles.heading: Disqualification of management personnel The Board of Directors is entitled to disqualify any member of senior management, at any
articles.text:
time during his or her career with the
institution of non-deposit-taking financial
service provider, if adverse information is later
revealed or if he or she acts in any manner
contrary to relevant laws and regulations or
acts in any manner detrimental to or not in the
best interest of the public in general.
Section 3: Common provisions for Board of
Directors and Management

articles.heading: Criteria for fit and proper (1) A member of the Board of Directors and of the management of a Non-Deposit-Taking
articles.text:
Financial Services Provider must satisfy
the requirement for honesty and integrity.
This includes –
(a) a person has not been sentenced to a term
of imprisonment equal to or exceeding six
months in a final judgement;
(b) no adverse information relating to any
financial or investment-related faults;
(c) a person has not contravened any
regulatory requirements or standards;
(d) a person has not been involved in any fault,
violation or regulatory breach that resulted
in the suspension or revocation of a license,
deregistration, or other enforcement action
against a company, partnership, or other
organisation by a competent regulatory or
governmental authority;
(e) a person has not been involved in any fault,
mismanagement, or regulatory breach that
resulted in insolvency, liquidation,
administration, or resolution proceedings
of a business;
(f) a person has not been dismissed,
disqualified, or resigned while under
investigation from any position in the
financial sector on account of any
misconduct;
(2) A member of the Board of Directors and of
the Non-Deposit-Taking Financial
Services Provider must have competence
and capability, including –
(a) qualifications, skills, and experience in
relevant financial operations
commensurate with the nature, scale, and
complexity of the activities of the NonDeposit-Taking Financial Services
Provider;
(b) appropriate professional training, technical
knowledge, and continuing professional
development relevant to the
responsibilities and functions the person is
expected to perform.
(c) sufficient availability and commitment to
effectively perform the responsibilities and
functions expected of the person.
(3) A member of the Board of Directors and a
member of Management of a Non-Deposit
Taking Financial Services Provider
demonstrate financial soundness. The
assessment is given to whether the person
–
(a) does not have any outstanding nonperforming loan or material overdue
financial obligation;
(b) has not been declared bankrupt or
insolvent;
(c) does not have any outstanding unpaid court
judgment, arbitral award, or similar legal
obligation;
(d) does not have a history of default on
financial obligations or persistent
delinquency;
(e) has not been subject to confiscation,
forfeiture, or attachment of assets arising
from unlawful conduct or failure to meet
legal obligations;
(f) does not have unresolved tax liabilities or
a history of persistent non-compliance with
tax obligations;
(g) is not subject to financial circumstances
that may expose the person to undue
influence, coercion, conflicts of interest, or
otherwise impair the person’s independent
judgment.
(4) For a shareholder, he or she must –
(a) be able to meet his or her debts as they fall
due and have a satisfactory credit report;
(b) has not been subject of any legally valid
judgment, debt or order that remains
outstanding or has not been satisfied within
a required period;
(c) a person has committed a fault with a
company, partnership or other organization
that lead to license revocation, withdrawal
or termination, or has been expelled by a
regulatory or government body;
(d) if it is a financial institution, appropriate
prudential solvency requirements are met;
(e) any other requirement that Central Bank
may deem necessary

articles.heading: Blacklisting (1) A non-deposit-taking financial services provider discloses to the Central Bank,
articles.text:
the names and complete addresses
including national identity card number
of any shareholder, director, member
of management or employee who has
committed embezzlement, fraud,
mismanagement, any other offense or
has demonstrated poor governance or
incompetence within his or her
institution. The incompetence referred
to in this Article is not applicable to a
shareholder.
(2) The submission of the list and
supporting documents of the persons
referred to in Paragraph (1), is done
within 30 days from confirmation of
the fault or taking the sanction by the
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider.
(3) Upon review of the information
submitted by non-deposit-taking
financial service provider and where it
is satisfied that the circumstances
justify such action, the Central Bank
blacklists the concerned person

articles.heading: Prohibition of blacklisted persons from serving A non-deposit-taking financial service provider is not allowed to appoint, nominate,
articles.text:
admit or employ a blacklisted person to serve
as a director, member of management,
shareholder or employee unless such person
has been rehabilitated by the Central Bank.

articles.heading: Rehabilitation (1) Any person who was dismissed by the Central Bank or non-deposit-taking financial services provider due to a
articles.text:
financial fault or misconduct in a
financial sector in a manner that he or
she is no longer fit and proper, may be
rehabilitated by the Central Bank five
years after the sanction.
(2) Rehabilitation after punishment for
misconduct other than dismissal is
done three years after the execution of
sanction where applicable or after the
cause that makes him or her not fit and
proper is known.
(3) The provisions of Paragraph (2) apply
also to staff who resigned while the
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider was conducting the
investigation on his or her behaviour
and the investigation concluded against
him or her.
(4) A repeat offender can only apply for
rehabilitation ten years after he or she
left the financial institution for
recurrent misconduct.

articles.heading: Application for rehabilitation
Criteria for rehabilitation The Central Bank may grant rehabilitation if it is satisfied with the following conditions
articles.text:
(a) the applicant paid damages or
restituted any property ordered by the
court;
(b) the applicant has shown continued
good behaviour and there is no adverse
information during and after the
punishment;
(c) the applicant complied with the
administrative sanction imposed;
(d) the applicant included in the
application file the document under
which he or she was dismissed or other
penalty was imposed;
(e) any other requirement that Central
Bank may deem necessary.

articles.heading: Decision on the application for rehabilitation (1) The Central Bank may grant rehabilitation after receiving the
articles.text:
opinion of all relevant institutions in
regard to fault which resulted into
dismissal or into the imposition of
another penalty if it is satisfied that the
concerned applicant has demonstrated
remorse and good behaviour.
(2) After considering the opinion referred
to in Paragraph (1), the Central Bank
can accept or reject the application for
rehabilitation.
(3) Upon receiving the complete file, the
Central Bank analyses the application
for rehabilitation and replies to the
applicant within 30 days.
(4) If the application is rejected due to nonobservance of the time provided for in

articles.heading: Responsibility of the Central Bank (1) The Central Bank carries out the regular supervision of non-deposittaking financial service provider to
articles.text:
ensure that they comply with the
provisions of this Regulation and other
frameworks put in place by the Central
Bank.
(2) The Central Bank exercises its
supervisory function through any or all
of the following methods:
(a) off-site analysis of documents and
information from the non-deposittaking financial service provider;
(b) on-site inspections;
(c) non prudential meetings with nondeposit-taking financial service
provider to discuss the prevailing
risks and their mitigation;
(d) any other lawful method that the
Central Bank considers
appropriate.
(3) The cost relating to the supervisory
function of the Central Bank is borne
by a supervised non-deposit-taking
financial services provider according to
the conditions determined in this
Regulation.

articles.heading: Off-site and on-site examination (1) The Central Bank or its appointee conducts an on-site examination of the
articles.text:
affairs of the non-deposit-taking
financial service providers whenever,
in its sole judgement, such an
examination is necessary in
determining the affairs of the
institution.
A
(2) An examination includes verification,
review, and audit, inspection of the
books, files and records of a nondeposit-taking financial service
provider in connection with its
business or financial affairs. It also
includes reproduction of the books,
files and records or parts thereof as well
as taking possession and keeping them
under the custody of the Central Bank
or its appointee after issuing proper
receipt thereon. In addition, it includes
interviewing the board members and
senior officials of the institution.

articles.heading: Consolidated supervision The Central Bank supervises each group of non-deposit-taking financial services provider
articles.text: on a consolidated basis.

articles.heading: Cross-border supervision (1) In case a parent company of a non- deposit-taking financial service
articles.text:
provider, is based in foreign country, or
a non-deposit-taking financial service
provider, has a subsidiary, a branch or
a representative office abroad, the
Central Bank may conclude a
memorandum of understanding with
the concerned regulator abroad to
enable the cross-border supervision
and sharing information.
(2) Pursuant to the memorandum of
understanding referred to in Paragraph
(1), the Central Bank supervises the
parent company, subsidiaries,
branches, and representative offices of
any Rwandan non-deposit-taking
financial service provider which are
established in a foreign country,
without prejudice to the power of the
supervisory authority of the host
country.
(3) Inspectors from the supervisory
authority of a foreign country may
exercise their duties in Rwanda with
regard to the supervision of the parent
company, subsidiaries, and
representative offices of a non-deposittaking financial service provider which
is established in their country, upon
prior written notification to the Central
Bank.

articles.heading: Facilitation to supervision The non-deposit-taking financial services provider ensures that there is no factor,
articles.text:
including unavailability or inadequacy of
information and lack of transparency, which
may hinder the conduct of investigation after
the submission of their application or inhibit
effective supervision after being licensed.

articles.heading: Annual supervision fee (1) After each financial year, a non-deposit financial service provider in category I
articles.text:
and category II is subject to payment of
a supervision fee of 0.05% of their
audited gross income generated in the
previous financial year. This amount is
paid not later than 30th April of the next
financial year for category I and II, and
not later than 31st January of each
following year for category III.
(2) The amount of the supervision fee
payable under Paragraph (1) cannot be
less than 1,000,000 FRW for category
I, and 500,000 FRW for category II.
(3) The supervision fee for category III is
FRW 100,000.

articles.heading: Report of inspection (1) The results of inspections conducted by the Central Bank are reported to the
articles.text:
Board of Directors of the non-deposittaking financial services provider.
Such results may also be forwarded to
external auditors.
(2) An inspected non-deposit-taking
financial services provider submits to
the Central Bank an action plan for
implementing all recommendations
agreed and discussed between the
representatives of the Central Bank and
A
the non-deposit-taking financial
services provider set out in the report.
The action plan indicates the deadline
within which each recommendation is
implemented.
(3) Failure to implement the Central Bank
recommendations may lead the Central
Bank to take a remedial action or
sanction against the concerned nondeposit-taking financial service
provider in accordance with the
provisions of this Regulation.

articles.heading: Actions for identified findings from the inspection (1) A non-deposit-taking financial service
articles.text:
provider takes appropriate measures
deemed necessary by the Central Bank
to rectify any unsound or unlawful
affair established as a result of an
examination authorized by the Central
Bank.
(2) The license of the non-deposit-taking
financial service provider may be
suspended or revoked by the Central
Bank if, in its judgement, the unsound
or the unlawful affair is not fully
rectified after the expiration of the
period allowed to the non-deposittaking financial service provider by the
Central Bank to do so.

articles.heading: Delegation of supervisory powers (1) For the effective exercise of its regulatory and supervisory functions
articles.text:
and powers under this Regulation and
subject to such conditions and
procedures as the Central Bank may
specifically prescribe, the Central Bank
may, through a memorandum of
understanding, delegate its supervisory
powers to a third party.
(2) The delegated third party complies
with the terms of the memorandum of
understanding, this Regulation, and of
other frameworks governing nondeposit-taking financial service
providers.
Section 2: Reporting and other supervisory
requirements

articles.heading: Financial reports (1) Any non-deposit-taking financial service provider prepares and submits
articles.text:
to the Central Bank its financial reports
prepared in accordance with the
generally accepted financial reporting
standards.
(2) The licensed non-deposit-taking
financial service provider submits to
the Central Bank quarterly report not
later than 10th of the following month.

articles.heading: Financial statements where a non-deposit-taking financial service provider is part of the group
articles.text:
A non-deposit-taking financial service
provider prepares separate financial statements
in case it is part of the group.

articles.heading: Key soundness indicators (1) The Central Bank may impose prudential requirements to a nondeposit-taking financial service
articles.text:
providers.
(2) However, for internal business
performance monitoring, the nondeposit-taking financial service
provider puts in place internal policy
aiming at measuring the soundness of
the business.
(3) The indicators that can be used
include –
(a) liquidity ratios;
(b) solvency ratios;
(c) gearing ratios;
(d) profitability ratios including return
on equity and return on assets;
(e) credit risk monitoring ratios,
including non-performing loans
ratio, single borrower’s limits,
insider lending limits, and ratios on
financing economic sectors.

articles.heading: External audit for category I and II (1) Any licensed non-deposit-taking financial service provider that falls
articles.text:
under category I and II is audited, each
year, by an external auditor that is on
the list of external auditors approved by
the Central Bank unless where
determined otherwise by this
Regulation.
(2) The audited financial statements of the
non-deposit-taking financial service
provider are submitted to the Central
Bank not later than 30th April following
the end of the financial year.

articles.heading: Other reports A directive may determine other reports to be submitted by the non-deposit-taking financial
articles.text: service provider to the Central Bank.

articles.heading: Documents and records keeping by a non-deposit-taking financial services provider (1) The non-deposit-taking financial
articles.text:
services provider depending on the
nature of its category, keeps some
or all of the following documents
at the office:
(a) license and approval documents;
(b) updated strategic plans, business
plans and action plans;
(c) internal policies and procedures;
(d) minutes of the Board and
management;
(e) finance and accounting records,
including the books of accounts,
tax documents, supporting
documents, etc;
(f) internal control reports;
(g) reports to Central Bank;
(h) lending documents, including loan
application, analysis and approval
documents, loan contracts, loan
restructuring documents, recovery
documents;
(i) loan classification reports: list of
borrowers, disbursement amount
and dates, payment amount and
dates, outstanding amount,
interests and penalties charged,
provisions constituted;
(j) collateral documents: loan
collateral certificates, if any,
guarantors’ information, collateral
registration and deregistration
information;
(k) human resources documents,
including recruitment documents,
staff job descriptions, staff codes
of conduct, staff contracts and
other staff files;
(l) other documents with third parties,
including borrowing contracts,
partnership contracts;
(m)other documents that deem
necessary.
(2) All documents and records must
be kept in a period not less than ten
years.

articles.heading: Confidentiality A non-deposit-taking financial services provider keeps confidential the information provided by the client and
articles.text:
does not disclose the information to a third
party without the written consent of the
client.
CHAPTER VI: SPECIFIC PROVISIONS
FOR CATEGORIES I AND II
Section One: Functioning of a non-deposittaking financial services provider under
category I and II

articles.heading: Composition and criteria for the board of directors (1) When selecting candidates for the composition of the Board of Directors,
Limit of cash use (1) The non-deposit-taking financial services provider discloses to the Central Bank the bank accounts
articles.text:
registered in the names of the business
through which all transactions are
conducted.
(2) Non-deposit-taking financial services
provider is prohibited to make cash
transactions during the disbursement of
the loan or loan repayment receipts.
Such transactions are conducted in
form of bank transfers, cheques or any
other payment instrument allowed by
the law or digital transactions and the
lending institution keeps evidence of
such transactions. However, cash
transactions may be done when a
customer has no formal channel, and
the transaction amount does not exceed
100,000 FRW.

articles.heading: Pricing model (1) Non-deposit-taking financial services provider must be transparent in pricing,
articles.text:
communicating the interest rate and
related fees and charges to the
borrower before signing loan contract.
(2) Non-deposit-taking financial services
provider must give the borrower key
facts statement, sign it and keep in the
client’s loan file.

articles.heading: Prohibited activities (1) A non-deposit-taking financial services provider does not take the following as
articles.text:
a collateral for borrowed money:
(a) National ID or passport;
(b) driving permit,
(c) cheques;
(d) ATM cards and security codes for
the ATM cards; or
(e) any other document establishing
the identity or nationality of the
holder.
(2) A non-deposit-taking financial service
provider does not hold or keep
borrower’s movable assets at the office
or any other any place as security for
borrowed money.
(3) A non-deposit-taking financial service
provider does not take client deposits.
(4) Lenders and borrowers must not sign
sale agreements for accessing credit
facilities instead of loan agreements.
(5) Lenders are not allowed to request
payment of compound interest.
(6) Lenders are not allowed to lend in
foreign currencies unless authorized by
the Central Bank.
(7) A license issued is not transferable or
assignable.
Section 2: Provisions relating to credit risk
management

articles.heading: Classification and provisioning for loans and commitments Credit and other commitments are classified
articles.text:
and provided for as follows:
(a) normal: current loans or commitments
with no delay or unpaid instalments. Its
provision 0% of the outstanding
balance net of eligible collaterals;
(b) watch: loans or commitments with at
least one or part of the instalment in
arrears for at least one day. Its
provision is 1% of the outstanding
balance net of eligible collaterals;
(c) substandard: loans or commitments
with at least one or part of the
instalment in arrears for at least 90
days. Its provision is 20% of the
outstanding balance net of eligible
collaterals;
(d) doubtful: loans or commitments with at
least one or part of the instalment in
arrears for at least 180 days. Its
provision is 50% of the outstanding
balance net of eligible collaterals;
(e) loss: loans and commitments with at
least one or part of the instalment in
arrears for at least 360 days. Its
provision is 100% of the outstanding
balance net of eligible collaterals.

articles.heading: Reclassification of credit category (1) A credit facility in “watch” category, is reclassified normal following the
articles.text:
repayment of all cumulated arrears
including principal and interests.
(2) A credit facility in substandard
category, is reclassified:
(a) “Watch” following the repayment of
all cumulated arrears principal and
interest;
(b) “normal” if the borrower remained
compliant with the repayment schedule
for next 2 consecutive instalments, as
from the time it was reclassified
“Watch”.
A
(3) A credit facility in doubtful category is
reclassified:
(a) “substandard” following the repayment
of all cumulated arrears including
principal and interest;
(b) “Watch” if the borrower remained
compliant with the repayment schedule
for next 2 consecutive instalments, as
from the time it was reclassified
“substandard”.
(c) “normal” if the borrower remained
compliant with the repayment schedule
for next 2 consecutive instalments, as
from the time it was reclassified
“watch”.
(4) A credit facility in “loss” category is
reclassified:
(a) “doubtful” following the repayment of
all cumulated arrears including
principal and interest;
(b) “substandard” if the borrower
remained compliant with the
repayment schedule for next 2
consecutive instalments, as from the
time it was reclassified “Doubtful”;
(c) “watch” if the borrower remained
compliant with the repayment schedule
for next 2 consecutive instalments, as
from the time it was reclassified
“substandard” until full repayment of
the loan facility.

articles.heading: Writing-off of the loan After approval of the Board of Directors, the loan with at least one or part of the instalment
articles.text:
in arrears for at least one year in loss category
is written off and kept off-balance sheet and is
placed under special recovery procedures.

articles.heading: Revision of risk classification of loans (1) The revision of the risk classification of loans when new or greater risks are
articles.text:
identified or weaknesses become
evident is done immediately, without
waiting for any scheduled periodic
review of the portfolio or individual
loan and must be documented in the
notes accompanying financial
statements.
(2) If a non-deposit-taking financial
services provider has more than one
loan or commitment with the same
borrower and any of the loans becomes
past due, all other loans to that
borrower and to the members in his or
her close relationship must be
considered past due and be classified
and provided for accordingly.

articles.heading: Interdiction to grant a credit facility A non-deposit-taking financial service provider does not grant a credit facility to a
articles.text:
borrower whose credit facility is still in
arrears within the same institution or any
other financial service provider unless he or
she has paid all arrears, including principal
and interests or the facility is restructured
and was put in normal or watch category.

articles.heading: Provisions as per International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS 9) (1) The Central Bank issues separate
articles.text:
guidelines related to provisions
required by International Financial
Reporting Standard (IFRS 9).
(2) To have enough allowance for asset
losses, a non-deposit-taking financial
services provider books the higher of
provisions recognized under
International Financial Reporting
Standard (IFRS 9) and the provisions
stated by these Regulations.

articles.heading: Effects of collateral on loan loss reserve Before providing for assets, a non-deposittaking financial services provider deducts
articles.text:
the value of eligible or qualifying collateral
or guarantee on the asset, exclusively as
follows:
(a) up to 100% of the value of cash
collateral;
(b) up to 100% of the value of securities
issued by the Government or the
Central Bank;
(c) up to 100% of the value of other
securities offered by the banks
operating in Rwanda;
(d) up to 60% of the net book value, after
depreciation and impairment, of duly
registered residential mortgages;
(e) up to 60% of the net book value, after
depreciation and impairment, of duly
registered commercial mortgages;
(f) up to 60% of the net book value, after
depreciation and impairment, of duly
registered land and other buildings;
(g) up to 40% of the net book value, after
depreciation and impairment, of
movable collaterals.

articles.heading: Restructured loans and other commitments (1) In those instances, where a member or a client is genuinely willing but unable
articles.text:
to repay his or her loan due to
circumstances beyond control such as
accident, external factors which may
cause adverse effects of the borrower’s
financed project, a non-deposit-taking
financial services provider may
restructure the terms of the loan or
commitment.
(2) The terms of the loan or commitment
that can be restructured include
repayment period, principal amount
and interest, collaterals, and other
terms of the contract.

articles.heading: Procedure for loan or commitment restructuring The following apply in case of the loan or commitment restructuring
articles.text:
(a) the analysis and approval of the loan or
commitment restructuring application
pass through the normal loan
processing procedures as determined
by a non-deposit-taking financial
service provider credit policy;
(b) the restructured loan is considered as a
new loan and is based on the new
contract;
(c) restructured loans are classified as
“watch” loans once new payments
begin on-time and in the agreed
amounts. In case the restructured loan
delays, it will pass through the normal
classification of loans and facilities;
(d) a non-deposit-taking financial services
provider sets in its internal policies
how the interests and penalties of the
restructured loans is computed;
(e) a non-deposit-taking financial services
provider keeps all information about
the circumstances justifying the
restructuring and keeps them in the
client or member’s files.

articles.heading: Moratorium period (1) The borrower may be provided with a moratorium period in special circumstances where his or her
articles.text:
financed project is abruptly affected by
adverse general economic conditions
or crisis or any other adverse
conditions beyond control.
(2) A non-deposit-taking financial services
provider defines in its internal policies,
the conditions for granting a
moratorium to the borrower.

articles.heading: Treatment of collaterals and guarantees by a non-deposit-taking financial services provider
articles.text:
(1) Any collateral that has been taken over
or acquired by a non-deposit-taking
financial services provider, available
for sale, is disposed of within a period
of three years from the date of the
effective takeover or acquisition.
(2) The value of asset to be treated in the
books of account must be the latest
market value of the asset after
deducting the applicable haircuts.
CHAPTER VII: ADMINISTRATIVE
SANCTIONS

articles.heading: Sanctions against non-deposittaking financial services provider A non-deposit-taking financial service
articles.text:
provider that violates the provisions of these
Regulations or a directive is liable to one or
more of the following sanctions, depending on
the gravity of the fault:
(a) written warning;
(b) written reprimand;
(c) suspension of any assistance from the
Central Bank;
(d) prohibition or suspension, for a certain
period of time, against carrying out
some operations or being subjected to
other limitations in the exercise of
activities;
(e) revocation of license.

articles.heading: Revocation of a license The Central Bank may revoke a non-deposit taking financial services provider’s license due
articles.text:
to at least one of the following reasons:
(a) failure to commence operations within
a period of 12 months from the date of
issuance of the license;
(b) cessation to conduct the authorized
activities without disclosing the
incident to the Central Bank in writing;
(c) deviation of capital in activities other
than those authorized by the Central
Bank;
(d) non-compliance with required paid-up
capital within the specified timeline;
(e) Conduct activities other than those
approved by the Central Bank;
(f) the shareholders of a non-deposittaking financial services provider, or a
non-deposit-taking financial services
provider itself, is convicted by any
court of competent jurisdiction, in
Rwanda or elsewhere, of an offense
related to money laundering, financing
terrorism and financing of proliferation
of weapons of mass destruction, or is
an affiliated or is a subsidiary of a
company that has been so convicted;
(g) if a non-deposit-taking financial
services provider has made a false or
incorrect statement in its application
for license;
(h) financing or involvement in illegal
practices;
(i) persistent non-compliance with
existing regulatory requirements;
(j) a non-deposit-taking financial services
provider becomes insolvent;
(k) failure to resume operations after the
period of suspension;
(l) in the Central Bank opinion, the nondeposit-taking financial service
provider operations negatively affect
the soundness of the financial sector
and the public interest.

articles.heading: Effects of license revocation (1) The effects on a non-deposit-taking financial services provider whose
articles.text:
license is revoked are the following:
(a) to be removed from the list of nondeposit-taking financial services
providers;
(b) to be subject to forced liquidation
in accordance with provisions of
this Regulation.
(2) In case of license revocation, the
Central Bank informs the regulated
financial service providers and the
public.

articles.heading: Suspension of operations of a non-deposit-taking financial services provider (1) The Central Bank is vested with the
articles.text:
authority to suspend a non-deposit-taking
financial services provider and its
operations for a period not exceeding six
months due to one of the following:
(a) recurrent misconduct following the
issuance of a written warning or
pecuniary sanctions;
(b) have issued a bouncing check;
(c) failure to maintain the minimum
working capital or required paid-up
capital following the issuance of a
warning letter;
(d) committed fraud cases;
(e) failure to provide information to the
Central Bank following the issuance
of a warning letter.
(2) The suspended a non-deposit-taking
financial services provider is required to –
(a) suspend its operations;
(b) remove all its advertisements or visible
signs.

articles.heading: Voluntary suspension of the business (1) The licensed non-deposit-taking financial services provider may request
articles.text:
in writing to the Central Bank to
suspend its activities, by submitting the
following documents:
(a) motives or reasons for suspension;
(b) how to manage assets and liabilities
under suspension period;
(c) the suspended non-deposit-taking
financial services provider applies, in
writing, for resuming suspended
activities at least two weeks before the
expiration of the suspension period.
(2) The suspension of the non-deposittaking financial services provider
activities cannot exceed three years.

articles.heading: Sanctions against directors, members of management or employees A director, a member of management or
Pecuniary sanctions (1) The Central Bank may, in addition to non-pecuniary sanctions provided for
articles.text:
in Articles 75 and 77, impose
pecuniary sanctions against a nondeposit-taking financial service
provider that violates this Regulation,
directives or decisions.
(2) The faults resulting in pecuniary
sanctions are specified in Annex IV.
(3) A non-deposit-taking financial services
provider that is subject to a fine must
pay it to the Central Bank within 30
days as from the date of notification of
the sanction.
(4) Subject to the provisions of this
Article, no pecuniary sanction can
exceed 2% of the minimum capital of a
non-deposit-taking financial service
provider set out by the regulation.
(5) The non-deposit-taking financial
services provider that does not pay the
pecuniary sanction at the account
indicated by Central Bank within the
time referred to in Paragraph (3), is
reported to the Credit Bureau and is
liable for 1% of the amount of sanction
per day of delay until the full payment.
(6) The non-deposit-taking financial
service provider may appeal to the
Governor of Central Bank on
pecuniary sanctions charged within
seven working days counted from the
date of receipt of the letter
communicating the sanction.
(7) The Governor decides on the appeal
referred to in Paragraph (6) within a
period of 30 days from the date of
receiving the written appeal. The
Governor’s decision on the appeal is
administratively final.
CHAPTER VIII: MISCELLANEOUS
PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Insolvency proceedings (1) A non-deposit-taking financial services provider does not commence any
articles.text:
action that leads to its insolvency or
voluntary liquidation without the
written approval of the Central Bank to
do so.
(2) The ability of the institution to pay all
its creditors without any delay
constitutes part of the consideration to
be considered by the Central Bank in
granting an approval for voluntary
liquidation.
(3) The authority for voluntary liquidation
is vested in the shareholders and
exercised at annual or extraordinary
general meeting.
(4) A non-deposit-taking financial services
provider enters into forced liquidation
when its license is revoked or it
becomes insolvent.

articles.heading: Mode of rendering financial services (1) A non-deposit-taking financial services provider may provide its financial
articles.text:
services either face to face or digitally.
(2) When a licensed non-deposit-taking
financial service provider intends to
change the model to digital services, it
must satisfy the conditions set out in

articles.heading: Issuance of specific implementing tools For enhanced implementation, the Central Bank may issue specific directive or guidelines
articles.text: concerning specific service.

articles.heading: Subscription to credit bureau A non-deposit taking financial services provider subscribes to credit bureau,
articles.text:
immediately after obtaining the license, to
assess the level of indebtedness of their clients,
where applicable.

articles.heading: Operating without Central Bank license Any person that conducts the service covered under these Regulations without authorization
articles.text:
from the Central Bank is punished in
accordance with relevant legislation.

articles.heading: Compliance with the new minimum paid up capital (1) Existing licensed non-deposit-taking financial services providers under
articles.text:
category II and III that were authorised
to provide services under special
category may continue offering those
services if they meet the requirements
for the new category comprising those
services.
(2) Existing non-deposit-taking financial
institutions that do not have the
minimum paid up capital at the date of
entry into force of this Regulation,
must meet it as follows:
(a) 375,000,000 FRW for non-deposittaking financial services providers
that are under category I, and
150,000,000 FRW for non-deposittaking financial services providers
that are under Category II within
two years from the date of entry
into force of this Regulation;
(b) 500,000,000 FRW for non-deposittaking financial services providers
that are under category I, and
200,000,000 FRW for non-deposittaking financial services providers
that are under Category II within
three years from the date of entry
into force of this Regulation.
(3) Existing licensed non-deposit-taking
financial institutions that do not meet
the minimum paid-up capital upon the
entry into force of this Regulation
submit to the Central Bank the buildup
capital plan within six months from the
entry into force of this Regulation.

articles.heading: Validation of existing licenses (1) Licenses issued and actions performed in accordance with Regulation no
articles.text:
65/04/2023 of 25/04/2023 governing
non-deposit-taking financial services
providers remain valid.
(2) However, existing non-deposit-taking
financial institutions whose services
are upgraded to a higher category in
accordance with this Regulation, must
apply to the Central Bank for alignment
within a period of 12 months from the
date of publication of this Regulation.
CHAPTER IX: FINAL PROVISIONS

articles.text: services providers is repealed.
